articles.title: El emotivo mensaje de Ilia Topuria a su hermano Aleksandre antes de su pelea
articles.standfirst: El mayor de los Topuria se enfrenta mañana a Santiago Luna en UFC Qatar
articles.summary: El mayor de los Topuria se enfrenta mañana a Santiago Luna en UFC Qatar
articles.body: Mañana es el día. Este sábado, Aleksandre Topuria (7-1) subirá a la jaula de UFC Qatar para buscar su tercer triunfo en UFC. Esta vez, ante el mexicano Santiago Luna (8-1). Y a su lado, en su esquina, estará su hermano Ilia Topuria. El doble campeón de la UFC, un año menor que Aleksandre, 'reaparece' en un acto de UFC desde que ambos, con los papeles intercambiados, abandonaron derrotados el jardín sur de la Casa Blanca. Por aquel entonces, fue el hombro de Aleksandre el que sostuvo a Ilia Topuria. Ahora es el 'Matador' el que actúa como apoyo para 'El Conquistador' en su ascenso hacia el título del peso gallo. Y en la previa, Ilia dedicó un emotivo texto en redes sociales a su hermano 'Sandro': "Hermano mío, quiero felicitarte por todo el trabajo, el sacrificio y la entrega que te han traído hasta aquí. Nadie en este mundo conoce mejor que nosotros el camino que hemos recorrido. Nadie sabe realmente lo que nos ha costado llegar hasta aquí, las dificultades que hemos superado, las veces que hemos tenido que levantarnos y todo lo que hemos dejado atrás para perseguir nuestros sueños. Todo empezó con dos hermanos que soñaban con tener una bicicleta para compartir. Y hoy, uno de esos niños se ha convertido en una inspiración para millones de personas. Pero lo que más me llena de orgullo no es lo que has conseguido, sino la persona en la que te has convertido. Porque yo sé quién eres, de dónde vienes y el corazón que hay detrás de cada batalla. Mañana no subes solo a ese octágono. Contigo suben nuestros sueños de niños, nuestros sacrificios, nuestra historia y todos los que nunca dejaron de creer en nosotros. Mañana la victoria te pertenece, porque te la has ganado con sangre, sudor y fuego. Pase lo que pase, para mí siempre serás un campeón, mi hermano mayor y uno de los mayores orgullos de mi vida. Te quiero con toda mi alma, hermano. Que Dios te acompañe mañana y siempre".

images.caption: Ilia y Aleksandre Topuria se abrazan. Sergi Lorenzo.

articles.title: Lauren Price beats Kotaskova to become undisputed world welterweight champion
articles.summary: Lauren Price dominates Michaela Kotaskova to seal her place in history by becoming undisputed world welterweight champion.
articles.body:
Lauren Price dominated Michaela Kotaskova to seal her place in history by becoming undisputed world welterweight champion.

Price, 32, took an unanimous, shut-out decision and the acclaim of the crowd to add the WBO title to her collection and become the first Welsh fighter to claim the accolade of holding all four major world titles.

Already an Olympic champion and world champion from her amateur days, it further underlined her claim as being among the very best in boxing.

But the way in which she did it, extending a perfect professional record to 11 wins from her 11 fights, suggested there could yet be more to come.

Price v Kotaskova: Watch undisputed title fight after Edwards v McGregor

History, hunger and headline bills - why Price is box office

Edwards' world title aim to join Welsh boxing greats

Price won every round from every judge in front of a partisan Cardiff crowd, producing an unrelenting pace that punished her opponent at every opportunity.

Although Price could not force a stoppage, there was never any doubt she had done enough against an opponent full of stamina and stubbornness.

Kotaskova, beaten only once, but never stopped in her career, showed real heart but had no answer to Price's expertise.

The Tokyo gold medal winner could celebrate even before the final bell sounded, climbing the corner ropes and into the record books.

It was lapped up by a sell-out Utilita Arena crowd who excitedly acknowledged the achievement and the moment.

Wales has produced 14 world champions, some of them genuine greats.

They include, of course, Joe Calzaghe who so often graced this venue with successful defence after successful defence of his super-middleweight crown.

He never reached undisputed status, though he was able to cross the capital city to go from arena to stadium champion.

That is the next challenge for Price, claiming before she left the ring that more is to come while talk immediately turned to five-weight world champion Claressa Shields as a stadium fight next summer.

That is for the future, but this was a night for history - with the calibre of some of the former boxers in the stands a nod to that.

Champions know champions. Five Welsh world title winners were in the capital to watch their compatriot do something never been done before.

From Cinderella Man Steve Robinson and Barry Jones, to the more recent Joe Cordina, who may still be eyeing a stadium return of his own in the coming weeks.

All have been proud to fly the flag, but perhaps none have worn it quite as much on their sleeve - or shorts - as Price has done.

Here, entering to the strains of a Welsh male voice choir, the atmosphere moved from Friday night in a city centre to full-blooded patriotism.

The anthem stirred so much Kotaskova couldn't help but raise an eyebrow before stepping out of her corner.

From then, she had no time to savour the moment let alone consider become an opportunity the Czech Republic's first world champion.

She felt flurries of punches from the first moments and struggled with the unrelenting pace set by the champion.

Steely-eyed, Price refused to allow a breath and, while Kotaskova continued to try and come onto the front foot, she was met by angry, but calculated attacks.

Kotaskova's problems only increased when she was cut in the fifth round, the hooks from the home fighter providing no let up.

At one point in the seventh, Kotaskova took a shot so fierce she almost turned her back to say no more, but still she came and still Price went hunting with hooks.

She could not find the decisive blow, finally letting the tempo slip, and even enjoying the final seconds as she accepted she had done more than enough to win and win a place in boxing history.

Edwards impresses in significant undercard win

Price was not the only Welsh winner on the night as Rhys Edwards secured a significant victory over Lee McGregor, taking an unanimous decision to claim the WBA Continental featherweight championship.

McGregor, 29, had stepped back down to featherweight after two defeats in his last three bouts and had made it clear he knew his chances of returning to world-challenging level was on the line.

His determination to keep coming forward showed what it meant, soaking up several clean shots, but Edwards proved too quick and too sharp.

The 26-year-old from Penygraig also had something to prove after a disappointing draw with Gully Powar last time out.

Then he faded in the latter round, but here Edwards managed to take McGregor's punches and maintain his own pace. It ensured what is perhaps the biggest win of his career, and to leave McGregor contemplating his options.

Elsewhere on the undercard, Willy Gilheaney's unbeaten record was taken away by the experience of Argentinean Alberto Igancio Palmetta, the former Olympic boxer showing plenty of know-how to overcome the Swansea fighter's guts and early control to take an unanimous points win.

Earlier in the night, Doncaster's Jake Goodwin took the decision in a game middleweight bout with Liverpool fighter Sean Arkwright. Goodwin – who had former world featherweight champion Josh Warrington in his corner – had only accepted the fight on two weeks' notice, accepting before he was even granted time off work.

And there were wins for Welsh fighters Brandon Scott and Kane Shepherd, while Cardigan's Josh Mellor and Newport's Lewis Howells fought to a draw.

articles.title: Machine Gun Shooting Mitchell Details Wild Hangout With Strickland
articles.summary: Bryce Mitchell has proven to be one of the wildest and most outspoken fighters on the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) roster, but even “Thug Nasty” had...
articles.body:
Bryce Mitchell has proven to be one of the wildest and most outspoken fighters on the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) roster, but even "Thug Nasty" had a tough time keeping up with UFC middleweight champion Sean Strickland during a recent hangout.

It's no secret that Mitchell and Strickland are two of the biggest UFC problem children. They say anything that is on their minds and it's usually controversial or derogatory to a specific group of people. UFC has continued to give both fighters a platform to speak and perform, which has given Mitchell and Strickland years to create drama. Strickland more so than Mitchell due to his championship tenure.

With all of that in mind, fight fans were intrigued to see how the two fighters would get along during a recent hangout. Mitchell visited Strickland in Las Vegas for a day of excitement, which included gun shooting, mixed martial arts (MMA) training, dirt bike riding, and basketball. Mitchell ended up having the "time of my life."

Check it out below and let us know if this is your idea of a day of fun!

"I had the time of my life," explained Mitchell during a recent Instagram post . "For the first time in my life I rode a dirt bike. I rode one a couple times, but not like I did yesterday.

"Fluffy was there, too. Fluffy coached me a lot. I was actually on Fluffy's bike and then we shot machine guns. Never shot a machine gun.

"It was awesome. I'm actually a pretty good shot with it. You just got to really hold that one down and hold that trigger and commit to it.

"And we also played a game of basketball. It was blacks versus whites. It was so fun though man.

articles.title: Kyoji Horiguchi vs. Asu Almabayev prediction, pick, start time, odds for UFC Qatar
articles.summary: Exciting flyweights Asu Almabayev and Kyoji Horiguchi could be in for a Fight of the Night in Qatar.
articles.body:
Kyoji Horiguchi and Asu Almabayev meet on the UFC Fight Night 294 main card at ABHA Arena in Doha, Qatar. Check out this quick breakdown of the matchup from MMA Junkie analyst Dan Tom.

Kyoji Horiguchi vs. Asu Almabayev UFC Fight Night 294 preview

Horiguchi (36-6 MMA, 9-2 UFC) aims to rebound from the first loss of his second UFC stint. After defeating Tagir Ulanbekov and Amir Albazi, Horiguchi lost a key matchup against Manel Kape in June.

Almabayev (24-3 MMA, 7-1 UFC) will look to make it four in a row. His current winning streak includes wins over Jose Ochoa, Alex Perez and Charles Johnson.

Kyoji Horiguchi vs. Asu Almabayev UFC Fight Night 294 expert pick, prediction

Filling out the main card is a men's flyweight attraction between ranked fighters, Kyoji Horiguchi and Asu Almabayev.

I'm happy to see this division being featured more prominently in 2026, and both Horiguchi and Almabayev are fighters deserving of the attention.

Almabayev has continued to make steady improvements off of his lone setback in the octagon, but I suspect that powerful strikers who can counter grapple still provide problems for the Kazakh fighter.

Horiguchi's defense is not beyond reproach, but the former UFC title challenger has made serious strides in his wrestling since moving shop to American Top Team and brings a wealth of experience into this matchup.

I expect a tight and tedious affair to score considering the styles and output at play, but I'll pick Horiguchi to edge out a decision win by landing the more meaningful and impactful offense.

Kyoji Horiguchi vs. Asu Almabayev UFC Fight Night 294 odds

The oddsmakers and the public favor the Japanese fighter, listing Horiguchi -188 and Almabayev +152 via FanDuel.

Kyoji Horiguchi vs. Asu Almabayev UFC Fight Night 294 start time, how to watch

Horiguchi and Almabayev are expected to walk to the cage at approximately 12:40 p.m. ET. The fight streams live on Paramount+ .

articles.title: El gran día de Aleksandre Topuria
articles.standfirst: 'El Conquistador' pelea esta tarde en Qatar (18.30h) ante el mexicano Santiago Luna
articles.summary: 'El Conquistador' pelea esta tarde en Qatar (18.30h) ante el mexicano Santiago Luna
articles.body: Un año después, Aleksandre Topuria (7-1) regresa al último octágono que pisó como peleador: el del Ali Bin Hamad al-Attiyah Arena, en Doha, Qatar. Allí, hace exactamente un año, venció a Almakhan en su segundo combate en la UFC. Ahora busca el pleno con su tercer triunfo en la mejor liga de MMA del mundo. Para ello, tendrá que superar este sábado (18.30 horas, aproximadamente, en Eurosport y HBO Max), al mexicano Santiago Luna (8-1). Será un choque de estilos precioso para cerrar la cartelera preliminar en un combate en el que el ganador quedará a las puertas del top-15 del peso gallo. Aleksandre Topuria, como demostró ante Thicknesse y Almakhan, es un peleador muy completo al que únicamente se le puede echar en cara no haber finalizado a ninguno de sus rivales. Pero el control y el dominio sobre ellos fue casi abosluto. Tras una larga inactividad derivada de su entrega como entrenador a la carrera de Ilia, posiblemente pelear dos combates completos era lo mejor que podía pasarle. "Tengo mi propia historia", explicaba en MARCA esta semana, lamentando no haber podido pelear más este año... cuando su objetivo era hacer, al menos, dos combates, como en 2025. Pero el objetivo no cambia: seguir escalando. "Es un rival más que lo tengo por delante y lo tengo que pasar por encima. Punto y final", desarrollaba. “La pelea verdadera es fuera del octágono. Al final, dentro son 15 o 25 minutos máximos. La pelea dónde tienes que mostrar lo que vales es realmente fuera. La pelea verdadera es la vida”, reflexionaba ‘El Conquistador’ horas antes de dar el peso, este viernes. Tanto él como Luna clavaron las 136 libras del peso gallo, oficializando el duelo de un evento que comandará el Prochazka vs Stirling y donde, por ejemplo, también estará el prometedor peleador argentino Kevin Vallejos. El hispanogeorgiano mantiene su filosofía: confía en sus posibilidades y sabe el trabajo que ha hecho durante todo el campamento. Y las apuestas, de forma clara además, están con él: es muy favorito. Luna, mientras, es un gran prospecto: viene de perder ante Bryce Mitchell (que fue arrasado en el pasado por Ilia Topuria), pero su inició fulgurante en la UFC no se ha apagado. Es un buen ‘wrestler’ (no al nivel de Aleksandre) y como todo peleador mexicano, peligroso en el boxeo. Una gran prueba para medir el nivel de Aleksandre.

images.caption: Aleksandre Topuria celebra su primer triunfo en UFC. UFC.
Aleksandre Topuria ante Santiago Luna. UFC.

articles.title: WOW 34 Valencia, un regreso histórico al Roig Arena
articles.standfirst: La compañía líder de MMA en España vuelve hoy al lugar donde batió todos los records el pasado sábado
articles.summary: La compañía líder de MMA en España vuelve hoy al lugar donde batió todos los records el pasado sábado
articles.body: Esta tarde, el Roig Arena volverá a vestirse de gala para albergar WOW 34 Valencia, un evento histórico en el que se llevarán a cabo varios combates de vital importancia para la compañía. En este mismo escenario, WOW FC batió el récord de asistencia a un evento de MMA en España el pasado abril, reuniendo a 14.000 espectadores en una velada para el recuerdo. En este ocasión se espera algo similar para que la compañía y las MMA en España sigan creciendo de manera exponencial como han hecho durante todo el año. En el combate estelar, Luis Iván Rodríguez (11-2) se medirá a Felipe Dos Santos (11-3) en un duelo que posiblemente decida al siguiente contendiente al título vacante de peso mosca. Tras la marcha de Fabià Sintes a la UFC no hay un campeón establecido en la división, y el peleador mexicano viene de superar notablemente a todo un mítico de la promotora como Davi Santos. Además, el peleador brasileño también busca volver a la UFC después de medirse a nombres de la talla de Lone'er Kavanagh, Manel Kape o André Lima. La pelea co estelar será la más emotiva de todas, ya que será el combate de retirada de Enrique 'Wasabi' Marín (14-8) ante César 'Goku' Arzamendia (9-7). El peleador español ha sido pionero en España en las MMA y es toda una leyenda, por lo que no hay mejor sitio en el que decir adiós que en un Roig Arena lleno hasta la bandera para despedir a una de las personas que ha permitido que las artes marciales mixtas evolucionen tanto en nuestro país. El evento también contará con otros grandes duelos, como el de Mor Dieye (5-0) ante Timur Kurbankadiev (6-1). El compañero de gimnasio de Joel Álvarez continúa invicto y ya venció a Nico Medina en el Roig Arena hace unos meses, por lo que buscará prolongar su récord invicto en busca de ganarse la pelea titular de una vez por todas. Además, otro que también estuvo presente en Valencia hace unos meses fue David Hervías (3-0), que en esta ocasión se enfrentará a Luis Hernández (6-1) para volver a demostrar por qué es uno de los mayores diamantes en bruto de las MMA españolas. En su debut en WOW FC David sufrió de lo lindo, y en esta ocasión volverá a tener un reto mayúsculo que le permita subir al siguiente escalón dentro de la compañía. Más allá de estos enfrentamientos, la cartelera también contará con otros grandes duelos como el de Dimitri Barkaia (1-0) vs Michele Balducci (1-1), el debut profesional de Mouslim Saidoulaev (0-0) ante Adonis Montero (0-1) o el combate entre Klim Gusyev (2-0) y Tome Bokofo (1-1), candidato a llevarse el bono de la noche. Otra velada que se espera que sea histórica y que se recordará durante mucho tiempo.

articles.title: UFC Qatar live results: Prochazka vs. Stirling updates, round-by-round scoring for today's fights
articles.summary: Follow UFC Qatar live results and round-by-round updates for the Jiri Prochazka vs. Navajo Stirling fight card on Saturday in Doha, Qatar.
articles.body: Uncrowned has UFC Qatar live results, round-by-round updates, highlights and start time for the Jiri Prochazka vs. Navajo Stirling fight card on Saturday at Ali Bin Hamad al-Attiyah Arena in Doha, Qatar. The UFC returns to Qatar for the second time in two years, bringing a 12-fight event headlined by a pivotal light heavyweight matchup between former champion Jiri Prochazka and undefeated rising contender Navajo Stirling.Procházka (32-6-1) enters Saturday's main event looking to rebound from a stunning April title loss to Carlos Ulberg. At age 34, the former UFC light heavyweight champion remains one of the division's most dangerous and unpredictable fighters, but another defeat could signficantly complicate his hopes of returning to title contention.Stirling (11-0) has quickly established himself among the 205-pound division's fastest-rising contenders. A City Kickboxing standout, the 28-year-old New Zealander has beaten his past three UFC opponents by stoppage, including ex-champ Jan Blachowicz.In the co-main event, former UFC bantamweight champion Aljamain Sterling (26-5) faces Argentine featherweight contender Kevin Vallejos (18-1).UFC Qatar starts at 10 a.m. ET with a seven-fight preliminary card, following by a five-fight main card at 1 p.m. ET.
